stories.title: Connectomic signatures advance the understandings of transdiagnostic heterogeneity in psychosis
stories.description: Current consensus-driven diagnostic systems poorly capture the marked heterogeneity and high comorbidity of psychiatric disorders, necessitating brain-based transdiagnostic frameworks to advance mechanistic understanding and clinical translation. Connectome-wide association studies have consistently identified widespread large-scale dysconnectivity across diagnostic boundaries, yet normative modeling and meta-analytic evidence highlights substantial inter-individual variability in the spatial topography and magnitude of connectomic deviations. In this Perspective, we bridge this divide between cross-disorder commonalities and individualized pathology by integrating connectomic overlap and computational biotyping into a top-down, four-tiered hierarchical architecture. This framework progresses from macro-scale transdiagnostic topological scaffolds, through meso-scale phenotypic triangulation, to data-driven biotypes and micro-scale clinical translations, delineating bidirectional interplay between shared network constraints and heterogeneous pathological diversification. Building on this architecture, we outline strategies leveraging multi-cohort data harmonization and healthy-anchored normative biotyping to refine robust cross-disorder circuits and reproducible neurobiotypes. Lastly, we propose a translational roadmap to transition connectomic stratification toward prospective, treatment-relevant clinical validation in precision psychiatry.

stories.title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
stories.description: Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1, co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy. Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) cause aggressive DMGs by preventing radial glial progenitor cell differentiation into oligodendrocytes. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor ASCL1 works with K27M to guide BRG1, maintaining cells in an oligodendrocyte precursor state.

stories.title: Phase-velocity disk model for predicting output-gap velocity distribution for the design of high-efficiency Klystrons
stories.description: Klystrons require continued efficiency improvement to satisfy the growing demands of energy efficiency in modern high power microwave and accelerator systems. At the output gap, the phase–velocity distribution of the bunched electron beam governs beam-to-RF energy extraction and thus strongly affects electronic efficiency. In this work, a disk-based prediction model is developed to evaluate the phase and velocity distribution of beam disks at the output gap and to estimate the corresponding energy extraction behaviour. A novel diagnostic quantity, cavity energy transfer ratio, is developed as a figure of merit of the work for cavity wise energy transfer diagnosis and klystron efficiency optimization. The model incorporates RF gap interaction, drift-space phase slippage, velocity modulation, and space-charge-influenced bunch evolution in a self-consistent framework. Two drift-length cases are investigated to examine the role of space-charge-dominated bunching in efficiency enhancement using this model. The longer-drift configuration produces stronger bunch evolution before the output cavity, and yields improved electronic efficiency. The predicted disk energy-extraction efficiency agrees closely with KLyC and CST results, validating the proposed approach for rapid efficiency evaluation in klystron design

stories.title: “Technology and science are, by definition, non-discriminatory”- narratives of the performance of sex and gender dimensions in European climate project proposals
stories.description: The integration of sex and gender dimensions (SGDs) in European research and innovation (R&I) funding has become a central policy priority, yet its practical implementation in grant proposals remains underexplored. This study investigates how SGDs are framed, negotiated, and operationalised in technology-oriented proposals addressing the climate crisis, submitted to Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe between 2014 and 2022. Using an inductive constructivist grounded theory approach, 87 funded and rejected proposals were analysed to identify patterns in SGDs integration. The findings reveal three main themes: (i) a wide spectrum of integration practices, ranging from comprehensive incorporation to more procedural or symbolic inclusion; (ii) differences in the use of terminology and conceptual clarity; and (iii) a tendency to conflate equal participation with SGDs in R&I, often focusing on women’s representation while overlooking broader structural dimensions. A tension emerges between formal compliance and substantive engagement, shaped by disciplinary norms, institutional expectations, and policy signals. The study provides a foundational understanding of how SGDs are currently addressed in EU grant writing and highlights areas where further support may be beneficial. These include enhanced training, clearer guidance, more transparent evaluation criteria, and greater institutional support. The findings offer useful insights for policymakers, funders, and researchers aiming to strengthen the integration of sex and gender considerations across the research funding landscape.

stories.title: Giant step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2
stories.description: Control of magnetization reversal is crucial for spintronic memory and logic devices. Previous studies on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets have largely treated magnetic regions in isolation, leaving the roles of step boundaries comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped Fe3GaTe2 using Kerr microscopy, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, and micromagnetic simulations. Our results indicate that step boundaries can serve as preferential sites for premature nucleation, giving rise to two distinct regimes. In Type I, reversal initiated in a thicker region propagates rapidly across the step boundary, reducing the coercivity of an adjacent thinner region by up to 59.3%. In Type II, stripe domains originating from the thicker region progressively enter the thinner region, shifting its critical switching field polarity and transforming its hysteresis loop from square to slanted, accompanied by a transition in the dominant reversal mode from rapid domain-wall motion to stripe domain growth. Similar behavior in Fe3GeTe2 suggests that step-boundary-mediated modulation may occur more broadly in layered van der Waals ferromagnets. Our findings highlight step engineering as a potential non-invasive strategy for designing efficient and thermally stable vdW spintronic devices. Boundaries can serve as nucleation points for magnetic domains, influencing the switching behavior. Here, Chen, Liu, Zhang, Chen and co-authors study magnetization reversal from stepped boundaries in van der Waals magnets, finding two distinct regimes of switching.

stories.title: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
stories.description: Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23–1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26–1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups. Disparities in cancer diagnosis amongst patients with disabilities remains a challenge, yet there are limited European population-based studies addressing such issue. Here, the authors show that in Northern Italy, people with disabilities, particularly those with mental and neuromuscular impairments are more likely to be diagnosed with non-metastatic cancers following emergency presentation and also have a higher one-year mortality rate compared to those without impairments.

stories.title: A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation
stories.description: Organ morphogenesis uses mechanotransduction feedback loops to convert forces into gene expression changes that regulate cell mechanics. How these loops integrate with developmental programs to ensure robust outcomes remains unclear. We show that Yap mechanotransduction establishes a self-limiting positive feedback loop for semicircular canal formation in zebrafish. Canal development proceeds through bud initiation, extension, and fusion within the otic epithelium. Local swelling of hyaluronan-rich extracellular matrix (ECM) in the bud activates Yap in a spatial pattern. Yap increases the expression of its target, ccn1l1, promoting further ECM expansion to sustain bud extension. This feedback loop confers developmental robustness: graded ccn1l1 knockdown reduces extension rate, yet canal formation persists and fails only with strong disruption. Critically, the loop contains its own termination mechanism. During bud fusion, PKA signaling, activated by the adhesion GPCR Adgrg6, downregulates ccn1l1, ending the loop. These findings reveal how mechanotransduction loops with built-in termination provide developmental control by integrating mechanical forces, transcriptional responses, and morphogenetic outcomes. Developing tissues must acquire the correct shape. This study shows that mechanical feedback between the extracellular matrix and Yap sustains timely tissue growth, while Adgrg6 terminates the feedback at the right time to ensure robust organ shape.

stories.title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
stories.description: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo12, which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo12-based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction. Piezoelectric materials enable bioelectronic sensing by converting mechanical stimuli into electrical signals. Xu et al. introduce intrinsically flexible polyoxometalate-based subnanowires and demonstrate their scalable integration into wireless wearable systems for human physiological monitoring.

stories.title: Inadequate school sanitation and mental health outcomes among adolescent and young adult girls in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India
stories.description: School infrastructure, particularly sex-specific toilet facilities, plays an important role in creating a safe and supportive learning environment for adolescent girls. Although inadequate or lack of school sanitation has been linked to poor educational outcomes, its relationship with girls’ mental health remains underexplored. This study examined the association between school toilet availability and mental health outcomes among adolescent and young adult girls using longitudinal data from two waves of the Understanding the Lives of Adolescents and Young Adults (UDAYA) survey in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India. The analysis included a pooled sample of 12,924 girls aged 10–23 years. The regression analysis from pooled OLS, between-effects and mixed-effects models consistently showed that girls attending schools without toilet facilities had significantly higher poor mental health scores after adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics. In contrast, the individual fixed-effects model showed no significant association, suggesting that the observed relationship is driven primarily by differences between girls rather than by within-individual changes in school toilet availability over time. Subgroup analyses further indicated that the association was more pronounced among girls residing in urban areas, those from Uttar Pradesh, and married or early-married girls, particularly during the second survey wave. Sensitivity analyses based on a balanced panel showed a similar pattern, as reported in the main findings. Supplementary findings further demonstrated that access to school toilet facilities was associated with higher odds of continued school enrolment. However, no significant association was observed with subsequent marriage after adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics. Findings suggest that the absence of school toilet facilities functions as a marker of broader educational and social disadvantage rather than a direct within-individual effect of school sanitation. Thus, strengthening school sanitation should be prioritised alongside broader investments in school infrastructure and supportive learning environments to improve girls’ educational participation and psychological well-being.

stories.title: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging
stories.description: Direct monitoring the multifaceted intracellular microenvironment is fundamental for deciphering localized cellular behavior and function. However, performing nanoscale spatiotemporal sensing of the dynamic physiochemical environment within a live cell has remained challenging, mainly limited by the lack of robust, biocompatible method which satisfies the requirements for spatiotemporal resolution, sensitivity, multi-physical sensing capability and long-term viability. Here we present a super-resolution-based quantum biosensing approach, namely Super-resolution Multi-physical field Imaging with Deconvolution, implemented in our custom-built setup which integrates nitrogen vacancy center-based quantum sensing with structured illumination microscopy. This enables quantitative, super-resolved, and long-term tracking of intracellular physical fields, featuring spatial resolution of 136 nm, temporal resolution of 150 ms, and field of view of 180×180 μm2. We further perform super-resolution multimodal imaging in a live cell, revealing the spatially heterogeneous reactive oxygen species dynamics under external stimulation. Our work enables the dynamic assessment of localized physiochemical dynamics under super-resolution quantum biosensing. This work presents a super-resolution quantum biosensing approach by integrating nitrogen vacancy (NV) center-based quantum nanodiamond sensors with structured illumination microscopy, which achieves super-resolution multi-physical imaging within live cells.

stories.title: White matter controllability at birth predicts social-emotional and language outcomes in toddlerhood
stories.description: The development of language and social-emotional skills is an important milestone supported by rapid brain maturation during early infancy. Deficits in these skills are hallmarks of several developmental disorders and have a prolonged impact on children’s lives. However, how white matter connections at birth support these complex skills is less well known. We investigated whether white matter at birth predicts social-emotional and language outcomes at toddlerhood in 530 infants. We used edge-centric network control theory to quantify edge controllability, or the ability of white-matter connections to drive transitions between diverse brain states, after birth. Connectome-based predictive modeling was used to predict the Quantitative Checklist for Autism in Toddlers (Q-CHAT) for social-emotional risks and the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development (BSID-III) for language skills at 18 months from the edge controllability data. We identified the social-emotional network (SEN) to predict Q-CHAT scores and the language network (LAN) to predict BSID-III scores. The SEN and LAN were complex, spanning the whole brain, but also significantly overlapped in anatomy and generalized across measures. Controllability in the SEN after birth partially mediated the association between Q-CHAT and BSID-III language scores at 18 months. Further, controllability in the SEN significantly differed between term and preterm infants and predicted Q-CHAT scores in an external sample of preterm infants. White matter controllability at birth predicts individual differences in social-emotional and language development at 18 months, revealing overlapping brain networks that emerge early in life. These networks may assist with identifying early risk for developmental delays and disorders.

stories.title: Orbital Hall conductivity in a d-wave altermagnet: a multi-orbital tight-binding study
stories.description: Altermagnets combine zero net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting, and their hallmark transport phenomenon—the spin-splitter effect—requires no spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Here we ask how the orbital degree of freedom fits into this picture. Using a minimal multi-orbital ($$t_{2g}$$) tight-binding model of a d-wave altermagnet with exact intra-$$t_{2g}$$ angular-momentum operators and the Kubo formalism, we compute on equal footing the charge, spin, and orbital Hall conductivities together with the dissipative Fermi-surface (“splitter”) spin and orbital responses. We uncover a duality between the two transport channels: in the Hall channel the orbital Hall conductivity is large and essentially independent of SOC while the spin Hall conductivity is purely SOC-induced; in the splitter channel the hierarchy is exactly reversed—the spin-splitter response is large and SOC-free, whereas its orbital counterpart vanishes identically in the SOC-free limit—a consequence of orbital-current quenching whenever the Hamiltonian admits a real matrix representation at every crystal momentum, verified explicitly for the microscopic models studied here, with the $$[C_2\Vert C_{4z}]$$ symmetry fixing the tensor structure once SOC is present—and is activated only by SOC. We verify the symmetry protection at machine precision, map the responses across the exchange–SOC parameter plane, and validate the model against spin-polarized density-functional calculations of RuO$$_2$$. Our results position d-wave altermagnets as tunable sources of orbital currents.
